London, 20<sup>th</sup> April 2009 



# Norilsk Nickel Daily News Digest 

**The EPA** has proposed a finding that greenhouse gases from new vehicles and industrial plants pose a danger to the public, kicking off a process that could result in tighter regulation of carbon dioxide emissions. The long-expected move by the EPA sets the stage for the agency to use its power to revisit the auto industry’s fuel economy standards.   Federal law already requires automakers to improve their average fleet fuel economy to 35 mpg by 2020. That’s a 40 percent improvement over current levels, and automakers fear standards could become even tougher.  The proposed EPA finding is to be published soon in the Federal Register, an action that will trigger a 60-day comment period. _Source: Automotive News_ 

**Declining** for the eleventh consecutive month, passenger car registrations in Europe fell by 9.0% in March compared to the same month last year. Over Q109, the market was down by 17.2% with a total of 3,439,720 new registrations compared to 4,154,778 units in the same period last year. **Western Europe** recorded 1,429,445 new passenger car registrations in March (-8.0%). The result was boosted by the 39.9% expansion of the German market, where consumers continued to respond widely to the government’s incentive scheme. Such a development underpinned the markets in France (+8.0%) and Italy (+0.2%). In the UK, registrations fell by 30.5%, reflecting the overall persisting lack of confidence in the economy. This sentiment also prevailed in Spain (-38.7%). In Q109 , the German market was the only one to post growth (+18.0%).  The downturn hit the Spanish (-43.1%) and the British (-29.7%) markets hardest. The Italian and French markets -were down 19.1% and -3.9%. Among the smaller markets, Luxemburg (-10.4%), Switzerland (-12.3%), Austria (-12.9%) and Belgium (-15.3%) performed best while Ireland and Iceland posted a decline of 64.9% and 91.3% respectively. **In the new EU Member States** , 76,803 new cars were registered in March, 25.4% less than last year. Poland and the Czech Republic posted a growth of 2.5% and 0.9% respectively. Slovakia also recorded a strong increase of 18.2% following the introduction of a scrapping scheme. For Q109, Poland consolidated its position as the largest market with a total of 87,939 new registrations and a 1.3% upturn. Latvia performed worst with a contraction by 77.9%. _Source:  ACEA_ 

**GM CEO** Fritz Henderson said the company has not decided whether to file for bankruptcy protection, but that preparations continue in case it is necessary.  He said he thinks a bankruptcy is probable. _Source:  Automotive News_ 

**Top auto executives** projected sales growth of up to 10%in China in 09. GM’s China CEO Kevin Wale expects China sales to grow 5-10% this year. Honda expects China sales to rise 10%, to 520,000 units. GM posted a nearly 25 % y-o-y rise in sales in China in March to 137,004 vehicles, a monthly record. China’s BYD Co

, a battery maker for electric cars expects auto sales to double to about 400,000 units. Source:  Bloomberg 

**Chongqing Changan Auto Co** ., Ford’s China partner, is planning acquisitions overseas as it prepares to enter Europe and North America where the industry downturn has hit hard, its chairman said.  “The longer the crisis lasts, the bigger the chance of failure or a scale-down of some American and European automakers,” Xu Liuping said.  “And that has provided a chance for entry by Chinese manufacturers”. Changan, China’s fourth-biggest auto maker, sold 306,500 vehicles in the first quarter, up 13% from a year earlier. The strong demand for its minivans and compact cars helped it contribute to a 3.88% first-quarter growth for the country’s overall vehicle market.  Sales reached 861,377 vehicles in 2008. **Guangzhou Automobile Group Co.** , the China partner of Toyota and Honda, will make acquisitions if needed, Manager Zeng Qinghong said; it will also consider forming more JVs  with foreign companies. _Source:  Automotive News / Bloomberg_
